newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Crude price gains boost Nigerian budget revenues.
newsitem.headline: Crude price gains boost Nigerian budget revenues.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has received $3.49 billion for sales of crude oil in the first six months of 1996 compared to the budgeted figure of $2.64 billion, the finance minister said on Thursday.
"The amount in excess of the price of $16 per barrel has been transferred to a special reserve," Anthony Ani said in his half-yearly review of budget performance.
Ani said the average selling price during the period under review had been $19.43 per barrel instead of the budgeted $16.00 per barrel.

Ani said income from the Petroleum Profit Tax for the six months under review amounted to $1.54 billion (33.9 billion naira) instead of a budgeted amount of $1.31 billion (28.7 billion naira). The government uses an exchange rate of $1=22 naira for official transactions.
Receipts for Petroleum Profit Tax in 1995 stood at 27.8 billion naira.
Nigeria receives over 95 percent of government revenues from its production of around two million barrels of crude oil per day.
